name: Paradeplatz
description: A square on Bahnhofstrasse lined with the head offices of Swiss banks, plus the Sprüngli café and chocolate shop.

name: Cabaret Voltaire
description: The small old-town venue where the Dada art movement started in 1916, now an arts space and bar with exhibitions and events.

name: Kunsthaus Zürich
description: Zurich’s main art museum, with Swiss and European painting and sculpture and a large collection of work by Alberto Giacometti.

name: Grossmünster
description: A twin-towered Romanesque church by the river, where Zwingli launched the Swiss Reformation in the 1520s. You can climb one of the towers.

name: Bürkliplatz
description: A square on the lake at the end of Bahnhofstrasse, where the lake boats leave and a flea market runs on Saturdays in summer.

name: Sechseläutenplatz
description: A big open square between the opera house and the lake, where a snowman effigy is burned at the Sechseläuten spring festival.

name: Rote Fabrik
description: A former silk mill on the lakeshore, turned into an alternative arts centre after 1980s protests, with concerts, theatre and a restaurant.

name: Burghölzli
description: The university psychiatric hospital on the edge of the city, where Carl Jung trained. It is a working hospital, not open to visitors.
